pr_title: EditorProperty: Fix missing increment buttons for integers

issue_context.title: 4.0.rc1, inc-decrement buttons missing from process priority input box
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.rc1.official [8843d9ad3]

### System information

Windows 10 22H2, Compatibility, Geforce GTX 550 Ti

### Issue description

The inc-decrement buttons are missing from the Process Priority input box.

The issue is observed in: v4.0.rc1.official [8843d9ad3]

![Godot_v4 0-rc1_win64_vzNcfx2YGm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13420573/218346770-cca6f609-48a6-4637-9731-cf631398e2f5.png)

The expected behavior is observed in: v3.5.2.rc2.official [1a2bf3eb4] and v3.5.1.stable.official [6fed1ffa3]

![Godot_v3 5 2-rc2_win64_LYSNq0gjW1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13420573/218346766-c68f1a21-307d-4ddd-b33a-9765a6a46988.png)


### Steps to reproduce

- open the attached project: [issue, inc-decrement buttons missing from process priority input box.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10717722/issue.inc-decrement.buttons.missing.from.process.priority.input.box.zip)

- in the `Inspector` panel, left-click on the `Process` property group to unfold it's properties.
Look at the `Priority` input box.

### Expected
There should be increment and decrement buttons on the right side of the input box.

### Observed
There are no increment and decrement buttons on the right side of the input box.


### Minimal reproduction project

### v4.0.rc1.official [8843d9ad3]

[issue, inc-decrement buttons missing from process priority input box.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10717722/issue.inc-decrement.buttons.missing.from.process.priority.input.box.zip)

### v3.5.2.rc2.official [1a2bf3eb4] and v3.5.1.stable.official [6fed1ffa3]

[inc-decrement buttons in process priority input box.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10717723/inc-decrement.buttons.in.process.priority.input.box.zip)
comments: I think priority is no longer an int, so that's why?

> I think priority is no longer an int, so that's why?

Probably not, this issue first occurred in v4.0.beta10.official [d0398f62f], there are multiple similar properties affected, such as `AnimatedSprite2D:frame`.

The setting lacks a property hint range (in both 4.0 and 3.x): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8c7b98d4526c6ba66d7f1636abb71ccbe54727c6/scene/main/node.cpp#L3016

I recommend something like `-4096,4096,1,or_less,or_greater`.

Well the problem is the default value:
```
	bool hide_slider = true;
```

`hide_slider` in `EditorSpinSlider` controls both the actual horizontal slider, and the up/down buttons.
*Edit:* Actually `EditorSpinSlider` changes behavior depending on the step. If the step is `1`, it shows increment/decrement, if it's different, it shows the slider. Hacky...

IMO the up/down buttons should always be shown for integer properties.

I remember that this was done intentionally because it was necessary to hide the button since the edit begining/finishing could not be determined. In other words, where a button is needed, a hint should be added.

review_comments:
There is no logic in the spin box "button" to notify edit_begin/edit_finish for recording the undo/redo correctly as was done in #69797.

I remember there was a problem with this, that every time a button is pressed in FPS mode, an undo redo is recorded. There are places where the buttons should be hidden, so if you want them to show by default, we need to add a negative hint like `"hide_button"` with separating this if statement from hide_slider https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69797/files#diff-1d3a3884c8e39e0b549397ed03359504d60dcaf695b52191a021b68a3dd38c9cR363.

This was previously hard-coded to force the button to be displayed when step is 1, so I made it possible to hide it by hide_slider. If diverting the hide_slider hint is a problem, it needs to be separated as a hide_button.

AFAIK this PR still respects the `hide_slider` hint in `PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE` handled right after, which will hide the buttons. This just sets the default for integers without a hint range and `hide_slider` hint. So if you want to hide the slider/buttons, you should use that hint.
Ah I see, I will test it.
